The public is hereby notified that the Shire of Harvey will be holding a Special Council Meeting in the Harvey Council Chambers, Young Street, Harvey on Tuesday, 9 June 2026 commencing at 4pm.

The purpose of this meeting is to appoint a Temporary Chief Executive Officer.

Confidentiality:

The associated report and Council’s discussion of the matter will be considered behind closed doors as the report contains confidential information that falls within the provisions of section 5.23(4)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995 and is not suitable for public disclosure.

All queries should be directed to Kourtney Williams, Manager Governance and Strategy, on 9729 0301 or governance@harvey.wa.gov.au.

Notice is hereby given that the Special Council Meeting of the Shire of Harvey Council, scheduled to be held on Tuesday, 12 May 2026 at 4pm at the Harvey Council Chambers, has been cancelled.

The meeting was originally convened to consider matters relating to Behavioural Complaints and the legislative framework.

The Shire is now seeking independent advice in relation to the legislative framework, and will reconvene a meeting of Council on receipt of that advice, either through the Ordinary Council Meeting cycle or by convening a Special Council Meeting for that purpose, if required.

All queries should be directed to Kourtney Williams, Manager Governance and Strategy, on 9729 0301 or governance@harvey.wa.gov.au.

The public is hereby notified that the Shire of Harvey will be holding a Special Ordinary Council Meeting in the Harvey Council Chambers, Young Street, Harvey on Tuesday, 12 May 2026 commencing at 4pm.

The purpose of this meeting is to enable Council to consider matters relating to the authorisation and determination of behavioural complaints in accordance with the Local Government (Model Code of Conduct) Regulations 2021.

The Agenda for the meeting will be made available on the Shire of Harvey website at least two days prior to the meeting.

The Shire of Harvey has welcomed a new Council term, following the 18 October 2025 Local Government Election.

Laurie Morley and Karen McCarthy have joined the Shire of Harvey Council. Meanwhile, Craig Carbone and Wendy Dickinson have been returned to their seats.

The new and returning Councillors were welcomed at a Swearing-In ceremony held Monday, 20 October 2025.

Shire of Harvey President Michelle Campbell said the new Council term would bring a great mix of governance experience, enthusiasm, and fresh thinking.

“It’s especially wonderful to see Council feature such strong representation from different communities within our Shire,” the Shire President said.

“Our newly Elected Members and returned Councillors bring perspectives from Harvey, Mornington, Leschenault and Brunswick Junction. I am sure this will further enrich Council decision-making and result in increasingly positive outcomes.

“I want to congratulate Cr Morley and Cr McCarthy on their appointment to Council.

I would also like to extend my congratulations to Cr Carbone and Cr Dickinson on being chosen once again to represent the community.”

After the Swearing-In Ceremony, a Special Council Meeting was held where Cr Craig Carbone was elected Deputy Shire President. Cr Carbone takes the baton from Cr John Bromham, who brought professionalism, positivity and a collaborative mindset to the role during his term.

Today, the Shire also farewelled outgoing Councillors James Junio, Dakota Krispyn and Joe Capogreco.

Shire President Michelle Campbell said their contributions had made a lasting impact on the community and it had been a pleasure to work with them.

“On behalf of Council, I’d like to acknowledge and thank former Councillors Junio, Krispyn and Capogreco for their service to the Harvey Region.

“I know our community will benefit for many years to come thanks to their insight, commitment and efforts while serving on Council.”

Over the next few weeks, the Shire of Harvey will deliver a variety of activities and presentations to support the new and returned Councillors.

This will include presentations on Budget planning and financial management processes, an introduction to the services the Shire provides, land use planning, Council planning and community engagement.

A bus tour to help Councillors familiarise themselves with facilities, projects and priorities across the Shire will also be arranged.

The Shire President said it would be both a busy and exciting period.

“We have the October Ordinary Council Meeting pencilled in, so right away Council 2025-2027 are getting stuck into it,” she said.

“I’m thrilled to begin this Council term with our new and returning Elected Members.

“I’m so excited for the year ahead and the opportunities we’ll have moving forward to make a positive impact across the Shire.”

Meet Council 2025-2027.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2025-05-30T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"We give a HOOT!"},"content":{"rendered":"

We have joined the owl-friendly movement!

So, what’s it all about?

Owls are very important to a healthy, balanced ecosystem. They help prevent the destruction of vegetation and farm crops by eating rodents. A family of barn owls can eat more than 1,000 rodents yearly!

Local governments and private landowners may control rodents using rodenticides. Some rodenticides are more harmful than others. If rodents consume especially harmful rodenticides, the owl may be harmed or killed. These especially harmful rodenticides are known as second-generation anticoagulant rodenticides or SGARS.

So, what we are doing?

We have been using first-generation anticoagulant rodenticides (FGARs) for quite some time.

These rodenticides are less likely to cause secondary poisoning in non-target animals.

Benefits can include:

  • Protecting owls
  • Reducing spread of disease
  • Increasing natural pest control (owls eating rodents)
  • Supporting biodiversity
  • Healthier gardens
  • Often cheaper to build an owl box to control rodents than to buy rodenticides

What’s changed?

At the 27 May 2025 Ordinary Council Meeting, Council voted to make us officially ‘owl-friendly.’

This means we’re going to continue to use FGARS and promote the benefits of better rodenticides across the Harvey Region.

The Shire welcomes three new and three returning members to Council following their success in the Local Government Elections 2023.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2023-10-09T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"Yarloop Workshops Project Update"},"content":{"rendered":"

The recommencement of the Stage 1 Redevelopment of the Yarloop Workshops Interpretation Centre has moved a step forward.

At a Special Meeting held Thursday, 5 October 2023, the Shire of Harvey Council authorised the Chief Executive Officer to proceed with directly engaging a suitably qualified contractor to secure and isolate the existing unfinished structures to prevent further degradation.

The decision was made as part of a recommendation not to award the tender for the Stage 1 Redevelopment to an outside contractor due to escalating cost variations. Instead, the Shire will investigate alternative options to reduce the overall costs of the Project to bring it in line with the allocated budget.

Shire President Paul Gillett said he is delighted with the decision, believing it to be within the public’s interest to maintain momentum on the Project.

“The Stage 1 Redevelopment of the Yarloop Workshops Interpretation Centre is an important economic driver project for Yarloop and the Harvey Region."

“It is great to be able to move this project forward again after it unfortunately stalled earlier this year when the contractor engaged by the Shire to deliver the project went into administration".

","protected":false}},{"date":"2023-08-11T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"2023-2024 Annual Budget"},"content":{"rendered":"

The Shire of Harvey is taking the next step towards a bright future with a smart and sustainable Budget that delivers ratepayers more bang for their buck.

Adopted last week at the 8 August Special Council Meeting, the 2023-2024 Annual Budget is a no-nonsense spending plan for the infrastructure, services and activities that make the Harvey Region a fantastic place to live.

Ratepayers will help power core services such as libraries, recreation centres, waste collection, community programs and more, as well as economy-building initiatives that bring visitors to the Region.

Shire of Harvey President Cr Paul Gillett said Council held multiple workshops and consulted with the community to strike the right Budget balance.

“This Budget reflects an economically tough international climate and the Harvey Region’s growing population,” Cr Gillett said.

“It also reflects the collaborative approach we took with the community to ensure the needs and interests of ratepayers are adequately supported.

“We’ve trimmed the fat  and are focusing solely on services, upgrades and high-quality projects that will accommodate our growing population.

“This Budget will progress exciting projects like the Ridley Place Foreshore Redevelopment and Harvey Skatepark, while also facilitating excellent services spanning road upgrades, parks maintenance, ranger activities and more.

“Budget highlights include $500,000 for new playgrounds across Galway Green and Portillo Lane in Binningup and more than $17 million in road construction and upgrades across the Harvey Region. We’re also going to create a public-transport friendly Treendale with $150,000 for bus shelters.”

The 2023-2024 Annual Budget is a $122 million package sourced primarily from smart investments and other revenue streams. Ratepayers contribute about $25 million.

Property owners will shortly be receiving Rates Notices and can visit the Shire of Harvey Rates webpage for up-to-date information about payments, including options for residents that need assistance.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2023-01-31T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"Shire of Harvey Libraries Literacy Festival 2023"},"content":{"rendered":"

Shire of Harvey Libraries will launch their first ever Literacy Festival on Thursday, 9-10 March 2023.

The exciting new event will bring some of Western Australia’s most intriguing creatives to Australind and Harvey Libraries for a series of workshops, Author Talks and family-friendly activities.

Included in the line-up is rural romance writer Fiona Palmer, crime writer Ian Hooper, Children’s Book Council Australia representative Jeanette Stampone and bestselling author Rachael Johns.

Short fiction writer Brooke Dunnell will also be visiting the Shire to discuss her work, as will Barry Award, Davitt Award, Ned Kelly Award and International Thriller Writer Award winner Dervla McTiernan.

Aside from meeting with experienced authors, locals will also have the opportunity to dive deep in their family’s history at the Australind Family History Society Open Day.

Families with young children are encouraged to bring their favourite teddy bear for the City of Bunbury Libraries Teddy Bear Roadshow at Ridley Place Australind Foreshore.

The event will feature Story Time, a Teddy Bears’ Picnic in a special tent, as well as face painting and playground play.

Also included in the packed program are events for the senior community, including afternoon tea and intergenerational storytelling at Harvey Library.

The Shire of Harvey Libraries Literacy Festival 2023 will bring a fresh and creative event to the local community and is designed to appeal to people of all ages.

Please visit the Libraries page to register for events.

You can also visit the Libraries page to download the Literacy Festival program or pick up a hard copy from Australind or Harvey Library.
 

","protected":false}},{"date":"2022-12-13T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"Yarloop Workshops project update"},"content":{"rendered":"

Shire of Harvey Council agreed to move ahead with Stage 1 of the Yarloop Workshops Redevelopment at a Special Council Meeting on Tuesday, 13 December 2022.

The contract for the development is currently with FIRM Construction Pty Ltd, but the company has recently entered voluntary administration.

Shire of Harvey Council President Paul Gillett said it was clear the Yarloop Project was important to the community, so Council decided to move quickly to progress the work.

“Council is working hard to get the Yarloop Workshops Redevelopment completed, and the Shire is working within the process to achieve a positive outcome for Stage 1 of the Project,” Cr Gillett said.

“We will provide updates along the way as further information comes to hand.”

The following motion was passed at the 13 December 2022 Special Council Meeting:

That Council, in relation to the Yarloop Workshops Project Stage 1:

  1. To authorise the Chief Executive Officer, following the obtaining of what is deemed to be sufficient information, and acting with appropriate external professional advice, to take the required steps to take any appropriate components of work out of the hands of the Contractor, and to engage existing sub-contractors or other parties directly to undertake that work.
     
  2. To the extent that the Chief Executive Officer exercises this authorisation, the Chief Executive Officer is exceptionally authorised to depart from the requirements of the Shire’s Purchasing Policy, Policy 2.2.11, clause 6.1.3 for expenditure thresholds under $250,000, where, by documented assessment, it is considered that the public interest in the momentum of the Project outweighs the desirability of multiple competitive quotes.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2022-10-31T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"JDAP Approves Binningup Development"},"content":{"rendered":"

The Joint Development Assessment Panel (JDAP) has approved the Albemarle Workers’ Accommodation Village in Binningup.

Albemarle Workers’ Accommodation is designed to accommodate 500 workers for the expansion of the nearby Albemarle Lithium Plant in Kemerton.

Shire of Harvey Council voted against the $73 million development at a Special Council Meeting on October 11.

Shire President Paul Gillett said the site was not suitable for the development.

However, JDAP was the determining authority for the application and approved the project on October 27,
subject to a range of conditions.

The Shire of Harvey will be receiving a full scope of the project shortly.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2022-10-12T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"Special Council Meeting outcome"},"content":{"rendered":"

Shire of Harvey Council has voted against the proposed $73 million Albemarle Workers’ Accommodation project in Binningup.

The decision was determined at the Special Council Meeting held at Harvey Town Hall on Tuesday, 11 October at 5pm.

Shire of Harvey President Paul Gillett said it was decided the site was not suitable for the proposed development.

“Council went with the Officer’s recommendation to refuse the application put forward for the Workers’ Accommodation project in Binningup,” Cr Gillett said.

“It was determined the location proposed for the project was not suitable.

“However, the application will be going to the [Joint Development Assessment Panel] for final determination.”

JDAP is the determining authority for this application and will decide whether the project is allowed to proceed.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2021-10-19T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"The Shire Welcomes New and Returning Councillors 2021"},"content":{"rendered":"

Newly elected Councillors Michelle Campbell, Michelle Boylan, Paul Gillett, Wendy Dickinson, Joe Capogreco and Dakota Krispyn were sworn in at a Special Council Meeting on Monday, 18 October 2021.

The Shire Council also voted in the new leaders with Councillor Paul Gillett re-elected as Harvey Shire President and Councillor Michelle Campbell taking on the role as Deputy Shire President.

Councillor Paul Gillett said it was encouraging to know he had the support of the community after being re-elected for his second term.

“I thank you for your support and look forward to continuing working with this exceptional Council to create positive outcomes for the community now and into the future,” Cr Gillett said.

He welcomed new Councillors Joe Capogreco and Dakota Krispyn to Council and said: “Welcome aboard, I’m sure you’ll enjoy being part of a cohesive and forward-thinking team working on our current and upcoming projects.”

Cr Gillett thanked outgoing Deputy President Francis Burgoyne for commitment to the Council over the past two years.

He also acknowledged retiring Councillors Derrick Simpson and Bill Adams thanking them for their dedication and commitment to the Council during many years of service.

Cr Campbell thanked the support of the community and Council after being re-elected for her second term and she was looking forward to filling the role as Deputy.

Councillors Michelle Boylan and Wendy Dickinson were also re-elected for another term.

View the results of the local government election held on Saturday, 16 October 2021.

","protected":false}},{"date":"2021-04-30T00:00:00","title":{"rendered":"Leschenault Leisure Centre Court Expansion"},"content":{"rendered":"

Council has endorsed a proposed upgrade of the Leschenault Leisure Centre indoor courts, subject to the availability of funding.

Shire of Harvey Council President Paul Gillett said this project was a key priority to ensure that we provide facilities that meet the needs of our growing population.

“We are one of the fastest growing local governments in the State with a projected population growth of more than 13,000 people in the next 10 -15 years.

“Upgrades to the Leschenault Leisure Centre are a crucial part of ensuring we have fit for purpose facilities to cater for the growing needs in our community.

“When you look at the statistics, 26 per cent of our population is children aged 5 to 15 years and 22 per cent of young people aged 15 to 24 years are overweight or obese. We need to provide the infrastructure to encourage physical activity.”

He said these upgrades would enhance the lives of people living in our community and this is important, especially when it’s related to physical and mental wellbeing.

Leschenault Leisure Centre Manager Richard Duke said these upgrades would allow the centre to expand its programs and attract country and regional competitions.

He said it would triple their seating capacity and provide a fit-for-purpose facility for wheel chair basketball and increase the number of sporting clubs who can play at the centre.

“These upgrades would support not only the Shire’s needs but the greater South West region would benefit, as we already are at capacity and need to ensure we are meeting the future projected population growth for the region.

“More than 20 teams just within the Shire utilise the centre and this does not include the wider region.

“For the first time ever we would be able to attract state and regional competitions, as the upgrades include full size courts which are compliant for basketball and netball.”

The upgrades include two additional courts, change rooms, disability access to courts and inclusion of a compliant accessible toilet and change room to court side.

There is an alternative ramped access to courts and a lift to mezzanine viewing area included in the plan, with improved spectator seating and fit for purpose food and beverage area overlooking the courts.
